summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped; simulation_allowed false). The paper (W4206159291) is a transient 3D FEniCS finite-element model of the Alpha EV6 floorplan, compared against a 3- and 5-mode POD reduced-order model. The extraction was labeled custom_2d_steady, but it has no blocks and no power_w, so the input gate failed ('A custom experiment needs 1–128 blocks and a power_w object'). A steady custom run would also have no transient trace, so it could not represent the paper's 3 ms pulsed workload. This is not a bundled EV6/GCC adaptation, and no Ascend910 or ATPlace pinned sizes were used, so no illustrative input.flp or one-row input.ptrace exists, and there is no source commit or placement assumption to report. The paper's observable is the hot-spot temperature rise in functional unit C versus time, plus x/y profiles at t = 3 ms. It exists only in figures, and no numeric value was extracted. Because Studio produced no output, nothing can be compared numerically. Even a hypothetical run could not be compared directly, because the location, aggregation, regime and boundary assumptions would not match. Qualitatively, the paper shows that 3 modes agree well with FEniCS and 5 modes are indistinguishable from it. That concerns POD accuracy, which Studio cannot test. Mismatches: (1) the 3D, 7-layer structure versus a 2D model; (2) a Robin bottom boundary with an unreported coefficient and adiabatic sides versus a Studio package stack; (3) a 3.333 us pulse train over 3 ms with unknown amplitude and duty cycle versus a one-row trace; (4) the POD-versus-DNS contribution versus a different solver; (5) rise above a 0 C ambient shown only in figures. The gate sets comparison_valid to false, and no exact replication is claimed.

The original is a 3D finite-element structure with 7 layers in z (Fig. 1b) and a substrate bottom Robin boundary. A 2D Studio model cannot represent this vertical conduction path.

The paper's cooling is a Robin boundary at the substrate bottom with an unreported heat transfer coefficient, and all other faces are adiabatic. This differs from any package, heat sink or interposer cooling stack in Studio.
The workload is a fast pulse train (3.333 us period, the average over 10k cycles at 3 GHz) simulated for 3 ms, with unreported amplitudes and duty cycle. A one-row power trace cannot reproduce it.
The paper's contribution is POD model order reduction (3 and 5 modes against the DNS). Studio uses a different solver, so POD accuracy and DoF reduction cannot be reproduced or compared.
There is no optimizer, controller or reliability analysis in the paper, so those aspects cannot be mapped to Studio.
Temperatures are reported as rise above a 0 C ambient and shown only in figures. They cannot be compared numerically with Studio output.
The packet does not specify the Studio package or material assumptions, so none are taken from the paper.
Any Studio run would use its own bundled package, materials and boundary conditions. These are not paper-derived and not equivalent to the FEniCS 3D stack.

Any placement and power trace would be a separate illustrative construction, because the paper gives block dimensions and powers only in Fig. 1, which is not numerically extractable. Generated coordinates must be kept distinct from paper facts.
Studio temperatures must not be compared numerically with the paper's POD or FEniCS results. No exact replication is claimed.
